description: Participating individually in the NASA Space Apps Challege 2026, working on lunar landing navigation.
summary:
The Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an advanced telemetry simulation and decision-support system developed in Java to evaluate and select optimal landing sites at the lunar South Pole. Addressing the complex challenges of lunar exploration, the software processes multi-variable parameters—including surface slope safety filters (>15° slope exclusion) and weighted scoring algorithms for solar illumination, Earth communication visibility, terrain roughness, and potential ice-water resources.

​By automating the filtering of hazardous craters and steep inclines, the system ensures safe and efficient trajectory planning for future lunar missions. This tool is critical for maximizing mission safety and resource utilization in high-risk lunar environments.
details:
The Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a Java-based simulation software that automates landing site selection at the lunar South Pole.

​It processes telemetry inputs, applies a strict safety filter for slopes exceeding 15°, and calculates an optimized score based on solar illumination, Earth communication visibility, terrain roughness, and ice-water resources.

​Tools: Developed in Java.

​Provides fast, objective, and safe mission-planning decisions for complex lunar environments.
